data.name: Muallim

data.long_meaning: The one who imparts knowledge or instructions. The name Muallim carries the meaning “Teacher, Instructor” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Muallim usually hope their child will grow to embody teacher, instructor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A guide on the spiritual path, a mentor who illuminates the way to Allah
data.etymology: Muallim belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Teacher, Instructor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muallim total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: معلم
in_arabic.meaning: اسم فاعل من علم، من يعلم الناس
in_arabic.long_meaning: معلم هو اسم مشتق من الفعل علم، ويعني الشخص الذي يعلم الناس أو يربيهم على شيء ما. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى من يقوم بتعليم الآخرين، سواء كان ذلك في مجال الدين أو العلوم الدنيوية. وقد وردت مشتقات هذا الفعل في القرآن الكريم، مثل قوله تعالى: "وَتُعَلِّمُونَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلُ" (النساء: 113)، حيث يشير إلى تعليم الناس الكتاب والوحي.

in_urdu.name: معلم
in_urdu.meaning: جو لوگوں کو تعلیم دیتا ہے، শিক্ষا دینے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: معلم (Muallim) کا مطلب ہے جو شخص لوگوں کو تعلیم دیتا ہے یا کسی فن کی تعلیم دیتا ہے۔ یہ نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، جہاں اس کا مطلب ہے 'علم سکھانے والا' یا 'تعلیم دینے والا'۔ اردو میں، یہ نام اکثر ایسے افراد کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو دین، تعلیم، یا کسی خاص فن میں مہارت رکھتے ہیں اور لوگوں کو اس کی تعلیم دیتے ہیں۔ تاریخی طور پر، معلم اسلامی تعلیم کے حوالے سے بھی استعمال ہوا ہے، جہاں اس کا مطلب ہے جو قرآن اور اسلامی علوم کی تعلیم دیتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुअल्लिम
in_hindi.meaning: जो लोगो को शिक्षा देता है, सिखाने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुअल्लिम (Muallim) का नाम अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है 'शिक्षक' या 'सिखाने वाला'। इस नाम का प्रयोग उन व्यक्तियों के लिए किया जाता है जो दूसरों को शिक्षा प्रदान करते हैं, चाहे वह धार्मिक शिक्षा हो या सांसारिक ज्ञान। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम उन लोगों के लिए सम्मानजनक तरीके से प्रयोग किया जाता है जो दूसरों को ज्ञान प्रदान करते हैं।

in_pashto.name: مُعَلِّم
in_pashto.meaning: چا کسانو ته زده کړي ورکوي، ښوونکی
in_pashto.long_meaning: مُعَلِّم (Muallim) په پښتو کې هغه څوک ته ویل کیږي چې نورو ته زده کړي ورکوي یا ښوونه کوي. دا نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چیرته چې دا 'ښوونکی' یا 'زده کړی ورکوونکی' معنی لري. په افغانستان او پښتونستان کې، دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي چې دیني زده کړو یا نورو علومو په برخه کې تخصص لري او خلکو ته يې زده کړي ورکوي.

in_english.name: Muallim
in_english.long_meaning: Muallim is an Arabic name that means 'teacher', 'educator', or 'one who teaches'. It is derived from the Arabic root 'a-l-m', which means 'to know' or 'to learn'. In Islamic tradition, Muallim is a title given to scholars and teachers who impart knowledge to others. The name has historical significance in Islamic education, particularly in the context of Quranic studies and Islamic sciences. As a given name, Muallim symbolizes wisdom, knowledge, and the ability to guide others.

data.cultural_impact: The name Muallim holds a significant place in the Islamic culture as it is closely associated with the propagation and sharing of knowledge. The word Muallim comes from the Arabic root letters "A-L-M" which means "to teach" or "to educate". Historically, Muallims were revered scholars and teachers in Islamic societies, who imparted wisdom, guidance, and knowledge to their students. They were not only educators but also moral guides, mentors, and spiritual leaders who helped shape the lives of their disciples.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Muallim carries immense importance as it represents the role of a guide and teacher in the spiritual journey towards Allah. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is known as the greatest Muallim, as he guided his followers towards the righteous path and imparted the teachings of Islam. By bestowing this name upon a child, parents express their hope and prayer that he or she will become a beacon of knowledge and wisdom, helping others in their spiritual quest for meaning and purpose in life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Teacher, Instructor" symbolizes The one who imparts knowledge or instructions. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Muallim serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of teacher, instructor.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Muallim al-Deccani, a renowned Islamic scholar and poet from the Deccan region of India, was a teacher ('muallim') to the famous Sufi saint, Baba Farid Ganj-i-shakar Chishti. Muallim al-Deccani is known for his Persian poetry, particularly his Diwan-e-Muallim (The Collection of Muallim), which contains Qasidas (poetic compositions) and Ghazals (lyric poems). This work has significantly influenced Urdu and Hindi poetry in the Indian subcontinent.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Sanani, also known as Muallim al-Sanani, was an Islamic scholar, theologian and jurist from the Sanan region of present-day Kazakhstan. He is known for his works in Hanafi jurisprudence and theology, particularly his al-Qawa'id al-Arba'ah fi Usul al-Fiqh (The Four Principles in Usul al-Fiqh). This work provides a comprehensive explanation of the foundational principles and methodology of Islamic law in the Hanafi school. Muallim al-Sanani's teachings have been influential in the Hanafi legal tradition throughout Central Asia and the Middle East.
